title: Pocket Clinic: Calm Care
premise: A vertical clinic management game where players expand a calm-care tower, process patients automatically, and unlock specialized treatment rooms to prevent unstable patients from turning violent.
interaction_model: Tap/click to build and upgrade rooms, tap rooms to open an upgrade modal, and drag vertically to scroll the tower while patients move and route autonomously.
objective: Earn Care Cash by treating patients, expand the tower with more clinics, unlock mental-care systems, and add calm suites so unstable patients are stabilized before they attack others.
progression: Start with reception and general clinics, scale income through new rooms and upgrades, unlock mental patients at level 25, unlock padded calm suites at level 28, then balance throughput and safety as specialized demand appears.
theme: Bright futuristic healthcare management with a soothing yet slightly chaotic mental-wellness twist.
mood: Polished, upbeat, accessible, and lightly tense once unstable patients begin escalating.
likely_audience: Casual mobile players who enjoy light tycoon, idle-management, and approachable hospital simulation games.
confidence_notes: High confidence in the build-upgrade-manage loop because it is explicit in the code and UI.
High confidence that room count functions as level/progression because unlocks and HUD messaging use room totals.
Moderate confidence that the intended fantasy is more arcade clinic management than strict hospital simulation due to simplified automated systems and soft penalties.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished mobile-first browser game called "Pocket Clinic: Calm Care," a casual vertical clinic-management tower builder played on one full-screen canvas with a glossy sci-fi medical HUD layered above it. The player starts with a reception room and some money, then taps a large "Open Clinic" button to buy new treatment rooms that stack upward floor by floor in a left-right alternating tower. Patients automatically spawn at the bottom, walk to reception, then get routed to idle rooms, treated over time, and leave while awarding cash. The player does not control characters directly; instead they manage the clinic by building more rooms, tapping rooms to open an upgrade modal, and purchasing two upgrade types for each room: speed to reduce treatment time and value to increase payout. Make the economy ramp upward with escalating room and upgrade costs, and let total room count act like the game level. Around level 25, introduce special mental-health patients whose sanity slowly decays while they wait. Show their condition through green, yellow, and red states. Yellow patients should prefer a specialized calm/padded suite if one exists; if they reach red, they should stop behaving like normal patients, become dangerous, chase another patient, trigger an impact event, and then both disappear as a soft penalty. Around level 28, unlock a second build button for calm suites that can stabilize these patients, restore them to calm, and still generate rewards. Include smooth vertical drag scrolling for the tower, floating reward and alert particles, subtle vibration/audio cues, animated danger/calm feedback badges, a pause-like upgrade modal, and a friendly futuristic presentation with cyan glass panels, white clinic rooms, readable labels, and a bright-to-soft gradient sky. The overall feeling should be approachable and satisfying like a light tycoon/management clicker, but with a small emergent triage system where growth and emotional stability must be balanced.
